department: Harvard-MIT Program in Health Sciences and Technology (HST)

deadline.value: Apply by December 1, 2026, 11:59 PM US Eastern (application opens September 1); official English test results must reach MIT by the deadline.
deadline.quote: Deadline: December 1 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time

gre_general.value: HST does not accept GRE (or MCAT) scores.
gre_general.quote: No, we do not accept GRE scores and will not consider GRE scores during the evaluation of your application.

gre_subject.quote: will not consider GRE scores during the evaluation of your application

english_waiver.value: An English-medium degree is not a ground for a waiver: HST considers waivers only for recent test results (taken on or after 8/31/2024) or a first/second-author peer-reviewed journal paper.
english_waiver.quote: Waivers: HST will consider waivers if official test results are within three years of matriculation (i.e. for fall 2027 enrollment exam date must be 8/31/2024 or later) or an applicant has a first or second author publication, from a major journal that is peer reviewed (conference papers not accepted).

supervisor.value: You need not name professors; HST asks applicants not to contact faculty until applications have been reviewed. Students can later work in any Harvard or MIT lab.
supervisor.quote: It is not necessary to name specific professors or labs you might want to join. HST requests that candiates wait to contact professors after applications have been reviewed.

funding.value: MEMP is fully funded: students in good standing get living expenses, tuition and health insurance for the whole PhD.
funding.quote: HST MEMP is a fully-funded program. Students in good academic standing receive financial support

entry_route.value: A bachelor's in engineering or a physical/quantitative science is expected; a master's is not required.
entry_route.quote: MEMP applicants should have an undergraduate (bachelors/baccalaureate) degree in an engineering discipline or a physical/quantitative science field (for example, chemistry, physics, computer science, computational neuroscience). A masters degree is not required.

notes: Joint Harvard-MIT PhD combining engineering/physical science with biomedical and clinical training; applicants need a quantitative background (a pure life-science degree is generally not enough). The HST FAQ says its fee waivers are for US citizens and permanent residents under OGE rules. Duolingo 135 and Cambridge 185 accepted.
name: Medical Engineering and Medical Physics (MEMP) PhD
